sanskrit: rāmas tu sahasaumitriḥ sutīkṣṇenābhipūjitaḥ pariṇamya niśāṃ tatra prabhāte pratyabudhyata
english: Rāma, together with Saumitri, having been honoured by Sutīkṣṇa, passed the night there and awoke at dawn.

sanskrit: utthāya tu yathākālaṃ rāghavaḥ saha sītayā upāspṛśat suśītena jalenotpalagandhinā
english: Rising at the proper hour, the Rāghava, together with Sītā, performed his ritual ablution with cool water fragrant with lotuses.

sanskrit: atha te 'gniṃ surāṃś caiva vaidehī rāmalakṣmaṇau kālyaṃ vidhivad abhyarcya tapasviśaraṇe vane
english: Then Vaidehī, Rāma, and Lakṣmaṇa duly worshipped the fire and the gods at dawn, in that forest hermitage of ascetics.

sanskrit: udayanntaṃ dinakaraṃ dṛṣṭvā vigatakalmaṣāḥ sutīkṣṇam abhigamyedaṃ ślakṣṇaṃ vacanam abruvan
english: Beholding the rising sun, freed from all impurity, they approached Sutīkṣṇa and spoke these gentle words.

sanskrit: sukhoṣitāḥ sma bhagavaṃs tvayā pūjyena pūjitāḥ āpṛcchāmaḥ prayāsyāmo munayas tvarayanti naḥ
english: "We have dwelt here in comfort, O reverend one, honoured by you who are yourself worthy of honour. We take our leave and must depart; the sages urge us on."

sanskrit: tvarāmahe vayaṃ draṣṭuṃ kṛtsnam āśramamaṇḍalam ṛṣīṇāṃ puṇyaśīlānāṃ daṇḍakāraṇyavāsinām
english: "We hasten to visit the entire circle of hermitages of those virtuous sages who dwell in the Daṇḍaka forest."

sanskrit: abhyanujñātum icchāmaḥ sahaibhir munipuṅgavaiḥ dharmanityais tapodāntair viśikhair iva pāvakaiḥ
english: "We wish to take leave of you along with these foremost of sages — ever steadfast in dharma, restrained through austerity, blazing like arrows of fire."

sanskrit: aviṣahyātapo yāvat sūryo nātivirājite amārgeṇāgatāṃ lakṣmīṃ prāpyevānvayavarjitaḥ
english: "While the sun has not yet blazed with unbearable heat — like a prosperity obtained by a crooked path yet unattained by those without lineage."

sanskrit: tāvad icchāmahe gantum ity uktvā caraṇau muneḥ vavande sahasaumitriḥ sītayā saha rāghavaḥ
english: "So long do we wish to go" — having spoken thus, the Rāghava, together with Saumitri and Sītā, bowed at the feet of the sage.

sanskrit: tau saṃspṛśantau caraṇāv utthāpya munipuṃgavaḥ gāḍham āliṅgya sasneham idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: The foremost of sages raised the two as they touched his feet, embraced them firmly with affection, and spoke these words.

sanskrit: ariṣṭaṃ gaccha panthānaṃ rāma saumitriṇā saha sītayā cānayā sārdhaṃ chāyayevānuvṛttayā
english: "Go your way without mishap, O Rāma, together with Saumitri and with this Sītā who follows you like your own shadow."

sanskrit: paśyāśramapadaṃ ramyaṃ daṇḍakāraṇyavāsinām eṣāṃ tapasvināṃ vīra tapasā bhāvitātmanām
english: "Visit the delightful hermitages of these ascetics who dwell in the Daṇḍaka forest, O hero — those whose souls have been purified by austerity."

sanskrit: suprājyaphalamūlāni puṣpitāni vanāni ca praśāntamṛgayūthāni śāntapakṣigaṇāni ca
english: "You shall see forests abundant with fruits and roots, in full flower, where herds of deer are tranquil and flocks of birds at peace."

sanskrit: phullapaṅkajaṣaḍāni prasannasalilāni ca kāraṇḍavavikīrṇāni taṭākāni sarāṃsi ca
english: "You shall see ponds and lakes with clusters of blooming lotuses, clear waters, scattered with kāraṇḍava ducks."

sanskrit: drakṣyase dṛṣṭiramyāṇi giriprasravaṇāni ca ramaṇīyāny araṇyāni mayūrābhirutāni ca
english: "You shall see mountain streams delightful to the eye, and charming forests resounding with the calls of peacocks."

sanskrit: gamyatāṃ vatsa saumitre bhavān api ca gacchatu āgantavyaṃ ca te dṛṣṭvā punar evāśramaṃ mama
english: "Go, my dear child; and you too, Saumitre, shall also go. After seeing all this, you must return again to my hermitage."

sanskrit: evam uktas tathety uktvā kākutsthaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ pradakṣiṇaṃ muniṃ kṛtā prasthātum upacakrame
english: Thus addressed, the Kākutstha replied "So be it," and together with Lakṣmaṇa, having circumambulated the sage, began to depart.

sanskrit: tataḥ śubhatare tūṇī dhanuṣī cāyatekṣaṇā dadau sītā tayor bhrātroḥ khaḍgau ca vimalau tataḥ
english: Then Sītā of the large eyes handed the two brothers their auspicious quivers and bows, and thereafter the two bright swords.

sanskrit: ābadhya ca śubhe tūṇī cāpe cādāya sasvane niṣkrāntāv āśramād gantum ubhau tau rāmalakṣmaṇau
english: Having strapped on the auspicious quivers and taken up the twanging bows, both Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa issued forth from the hermitage to go.

sanskrit: sutīkṣṇenābhyanujñātaṃ prasthitaṃ raghunandanam vaidehī snigdhayā vācā bhartāram idam abravīt
english: As Raghunandana set out, having been given leave by Sutīkṣṇa, Vaidehī spoke these words to her husband in an affectionate voice.

sanskrit: ayaṃ dharmaḥ susūkṣmeṇa vidhinā prāpyate mahān nivṛttena ca śakyo 'yaṃ vyasanāt kāmajād iha
english: "This great dharma is attained by an exceedingly subtle discipline; it is achievable here by one who has turned away from the vices born of desire."

sanskrit: trīṇy eva vyasanāni atra kāmajāni bhavanty uta mithyā vākyaṃ paramakaṃ tasmād gurutarāv ubhau paradārābhigamanaṃ vinā vairaṃ ca raudratā
english: "There are precisely three vices arising from desire: false speech, which is the foremost; and graver than that, the other two — approaching another's wife, and violent cruelty without enmity."

sanskrit: mithyāvākyaṃ na te bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati rāghava kuto 'bhilaṣaṇaṃ strīṇāṃ pareṣāṃ dharmanāśanam
english: "False speech has never been nor will ever be in you, O Rāghava; still less the desire for other men's wives, which destroys dharma."

sanskrit: tac ca sarvaṃ mahābāho śakyaṃ voḍhuṃ jitendriyaiḥ tava vaśyendriyatvaṃ ca jānāmi śubhadarśana
english: "All of this, O mighty-armed one, can be borne by those who have mastered their senses; and I know that your senses are indeed under your control, O fair to behold."

sanskrit: tṛtīyaṃ yad idaṃ raudraṃ paraprāṇābhihiṃsanam nirvairaṃ kriyate mohāt tac ca te samupasthitam
english: "But this third vice, the terrible injury to the lives of others, done without enmity out of delusion — that is now upon you."

sanskrit: pratijñātas tvayā vīra daṇḍakāraṇyavāsinām ṛṣīṇāṃ rakṣaṇārthāya vadhaḥ saṃyati rakṣasām
english: "You have pledged, O hero, to slay the rākṣasas in battle for the protection of the sages who dwell in the Daṇḍaka forest."

sanskrit: etannimittaṃ ca vanaṃ daṇḍakā iti viśrutam prasthitas tvaṃ saha bhrātrā dhṛtabāṇaśarāsanaḥ
english: "It is for this reason that you set out with your brother into the forest renowned as Daṇḍaka, bearing arrows and bow."

sanskrit: tatas tvāṃ prasthitaṃ dṛṣṭvā mama cintākulaṃ manaḥ tvad vṛttaṃ cintayantyā vai bhaven niḥśreyasaṃ hitam
english: "Seeing you thus set out, my mind is filled with anxiety; pondering on what befits you, let me speak what may be for your highest good."

sanskrit: na hi me rocate vīra gamanaṃ daṇḍakān prati kāraṇaṃ tatra vakṣyāmi vadantyāḥ śrūyatāṃ mama
english: "I do not approve of your going into the Daṇḍaka, O hero; hear the reason I shall state as I speak."

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi bāṇadhanuṣpāṇir bhrātrā saha vanaṃ gataḥ dṛṣṭvā vanacarān sarvān kaccit kuryāḥ śaravyayam
english: "You have gone into the forest bearing arrows and bow in hand, with your brother; seeing all the forest-dwellers, might you not spend your arrows freely?"

sanskrit: kṣatriyāṇām iha dhanur hutāśasyendhanāni ca samīpataḥ sthitaṃ tejobalam ucchrayate bhṛśam
english: "For warriors here, the bow and the fuel of fire standing near one another greatly inflame the power of that energy."

sanskrit: purā kila mahābāho tapasvī satyavāk śuciḥ kasmiṃś cid abhavat puṇye vane ratamṛgadvije
english: "Long ago, O mighty-armed one, there was, they say, an ascetic — truthful, pure — who delighted in deer and birds in a certain sacred forest."

sanskrit: tasyaiva tapaso vighnaṃ kartum indraḥ śacīpatiḥ khaḍgapāṇir athāgacchad āśramaṃ bhaṭa rūpadhṛk
english: "To create an obstacle to his austerity, Indra, the lord of Śacī, came to the hermitage in the guise of a soldier, sword in hand."

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tad āśramapade nihitaḥ khaḍga uttamaḥ sa nyāsavidhinā dattaḥ puṇye tapasi tiṣṭhataḥ
english: "That excellent sword was left in the hermitage grounds; it was given as a deposit in trust to him who persevered in his sacred austerity."

sanskrit: sa tac chastram anuprāpya nyāsarakṣaṇatatparaḥ vane tu vicaraty eva rakṣan pratyayam ātmanaḥ
english: "Having received that weapon, intent on guarding the deposit, he wandered through the forest carrying it, protecting the trust placed in him."

sanskrit: yatra gacchaty upādātuṃ mūlāni ca phalāni ca na vinā yāti taṃ khaḍgaṃ nyāsarakṣaṇatatparaḥ
english: "Wherever he went to gather roots and fruits, he would not go without that sword, so intent was he on guarding the deposit."

sanskrit: nityaṃ śastraṃ parivahan krameṇa sa tapodhanaḥ cakāra raudrīṃ svāṃ buddhiṃ tyaktvā tapasi niścayam
english: "Constantly carrying the weapon, that ascetic, rich in austerity, gradually developed a fierce disposition, abandoning his resolve in austerity."

sanskrit: tataḥ sa raudrābhirataḥ pramatto 'dharmakarṣitaḥ tasya śastrasya saṃvāsāj jagāma narakaṃ muniḥ
english: "Then that sage, addicted to violence, heedless, dragged down by adharma, went to hell through constant association with that weapon."

sanskrit: snehāc ca bahumānāc ca smāraye tvāṃ na śikṣaye na kathaṃ cana sā kāryā hṛhītadhanuṣā tvayā
english: "Out of love and deep respect I remind you, not instruct you: that disposition should in no way be entertained by you who have taken up the bow."

sanskrit: buddhir vairaṃ vinā hantuṃ rākṣasān daṇḍakāśritān aparādhaṃ vinā hantuṃ lokān vīra na kāmaye
english: "I do not wish, O hero, for the thought of slaying the rākṣasas sheltering in the Daṇḍaka without cause, or of slaying people without offence."

sanskrit: kṣatriyāṇāṃ tu vīrāṇāṃ vaneṣu niyatātmanām dhanuṣā kāryam etāvad ārtānām abhirakṣaṇam
english: "For heroic warriors living in the forests with disciplined minds, the purpose of the bow is only this: to protect those in distress."

sanskrit: kva ca śastraṃ kva ca vanaṃ kva ca kṣātraṃ tapaḥ kva ca vyāviddham idam asmābhir deśadharmas tu pūjyatām
english: "What place has the weapon here? What place has the forest? What place the warrior's dharma, and what place austerity? These are discordant — let the duty of the place be honoured."

sanskrit: tad āryakaluṣā buddhir jāyate śastrasevanāt punar gatvā tv ayodhyāyāṃ kṣatradharmaṃ cariṣyasi
english: "That intellect becomes tainted of its nobility through resort to weapons; when you return to Ayodhyā you will practise the warrior's dharma again."

sanskrit: akṣayā tu bhavet prītiḥ śvaśrū śvaśurayor mama yadi rājyaṃ hi saṃnyasya bhaves tvaṃ nirato muniḥ
english: "The delight of my mothers-in-law and father-in-law would be undying if you were to renounce the kingdom and become a devoted sage."

sanskrit: dharmād arthaḥ prabhavati dharmāt prabhavate sukham dharmeṇa labhate sarvaṃ dharmasāram idaṃ jagat
english: "From dharma arises wealth; from dharma happiness arises; through dharma all is obtained — dharma is the essence of this world."

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ niyamais tais taiḥ karṣayitvā prayatnataḥ prāpyate nipuṇair dharmo na sukhāl labhyate sukham
english: "Dharma is attained by the wise through diligent self-mortification by various restraints; happiness is not obtained from happiness alone."

sanskrit: nityaṃ śucimatiḥ saumya cara dharmaṃ tapovane sarvaṃ hi viditaṃ tubhyaṃ trailokyam api tattvataḥ
english: "Ever of pure mind, O gentle one, practise dharma in this forest of austerity; for all the three worlds are truly known to you in their essence."

sanskrit: strīcāpalād etad udāhṛtaṃ me dharmaṃ ca vaktuṃ tava kaḥ samarthaḥ vicārya buddhyā tu sahānujena yad rocate tat kuru mācireṇa
english: "This has been spoken by me out of a woman's impulsiveness; who indeed is capable of instructing you in dharma? Reflecting with your brother, do what seems fit without delay."

sanskrit: vākyam etat tu vaidehyā vyāhṛtaṃ bhartṛbhaktayā śrutvā dharme sthito rāmaḥ pratyuvācātha maithilīm
english: Hearing these words thus spoken by Vaidehī who was devoted to her husband, Rāma, established in dharma, replied to the Maithilī.

sanskrit: hitam uktaṃ tvayā devi snigdhayā sadṛśaṃ vacaḥ kulaṃ vyapadiśantyā ca dharmajñe janakātmaje
english: "What is beneficial has been spoken by you, O queen, words befitting your affection and reflecting your noble lineage, O daughter of Janaka, knower of dharma."

sanskrit: kiṃ tu vakṣyāmy ahaṃ devi tvayaivoktam idaṃ vacaḥ kṣatriyair dhāryate cāpo nārtaśabdo bhaved iti
english: "But I shall say, O queen, what you yourself have stated: warriors bear the bow so that the cry of distress shall not be heard."

sanskrit: te cārtā daṇḍakāraṇye munayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ māṃ sīte svayam āgamya śaraṇyāḥ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ
english: "And those sages in the Daṇḍaka forest, O Sītā, afflicted and firm in their vows, have themselves come to me — those deserving refuge have sought my refuge."

sanskrit: vasanto dharmaniratā vane mūlaphalāśanāḥ na labhante sukhaṃ bhītā rākṣasaiḥ krūrakarmabhiḥ
english: "Dwelling in the forest devoted to dharma, subsisting on roots and fruits, they find no peace, frightened by the rākṣasas of cruel deeds."

sanskrit: kāle kāle ca niratā niyamair vividhair vane bhakṣyante rākṣasair bhīmair naramāṃsopajīvibhiḥ
english: "Though engaged season by season in various restraints in the forest, they are devoured by terrible rākṣasas who live upon human flesh."

sanskrit: te bhakṣyamāṇā munayo daṇḍakāraṇyavāsinaḥ asmān abhyavapadyeti mām ūcur dvijasattamāḥ
english: "Those sages dwelling in the Daṇḍaka forest, being thus devoured, said to me — those best of twice-born: 'Come to our aid.'"

sanskrit: mayā tu vacanaṃ śrutvā teṣām evaṃ mukhāc cyutam kṛtvā caraṇaśuśrūṣāṃ vākyam etad udāhṛtam
english: "I, having heard these words thus fallen from their lips, paid reverence at their feet and spoke this reply."

sanskrit: prasīdantu bhavanto me hrīr eṣā hi mamātulā yadīdṛśair ahaṃ viprair upastheyair upasthitaḥ kiṃ karomīti ca mayā vyāhṛtaṃ dvijasaṃnidhau
english: "'May your honours be gracious to me — this shame of mine is incomparable, that those such as you brāhmaṇas, whom I should approach, have had to approach me.' And I said in the assembly of twice-born: 'What shall I do?'"

sanskrit: sarvair eva samāgamya vāg iyaṃ samudāhṛtā rākṣasair daṇḍakāraṇye bahubhiḥ kāmarūpibhiḥ arditāḥ sma bhṛśaṃ rāma bhavān nas trātum arhati
english: "Then all of them together uttered this speech: 'We are greatly oppressed in the Daṇḍaka forest by the many rākṣasas who change form at will, O Rāma; you are worthy to protect us.'"

sanskrit: homakāle tu saṃprāpte parvakāleṣu cānagha dharṣayanti sma durdharṣā rākṣasāḥ piśitāśanāḥ
english: "When the time for the fire-oblation arrives and at the times of sacred rites, O sinless one, those unconquerable rākṣasas who feed on flesh assail us."

sanskrit: rākṣasair dharṣitānāṃ ca tāpasānāṃ tapasvinām gatiṃ mṛgayamāṇānāṃ bhavān naḥ paramā gatiḥ
english: "For us ascetics, those practitioners of austerity who are harassed by rākṣasas and seek a course of refuge, you are the highest refuge."

sanskrit: kāmaṃ tapaḥ prabhāvena śaktā hantuṃ niśācarān cirārjitaṃ tu necchāmas tapaḥ khaṇḍayituṃ vayam
english: "By the power of austerity we are indeed capable of slaying the night-wanderers; but we do not wish to squander the austerity long accumulated."

sanskrit: bahuvighnaṃ taponityaṃ duścaraṃ caiva rāghava tena śāpaṃ na muñcāmo bhakṣyamāṇāś ca rākṣasaiḥ
english: "Austerity, O Rāghava, is beset with many obstacles and is hard to perform; therefore we do not release a curse even as we are being devoured by the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: tad ardyamānān rakṣobhir daṇḍakāraṇyavāsibhiḥ rakṣanas tvaṃ saha bhrātrā tvannāthā hi vayaṃ vane
english: "Therefore protect us as we are tormented by the rākṣasas who dwell in the Daṇḍaka forest, you together with your brother — for we have no lord but you in the forest."

sanskrit: mayā caitad vacaḥ śrutvā kārtsnyena paripālanam ṛṣīṇāṃ daṇḍakāraṇye saṃśrutaṃ janakātmaje
english: "And I, having heard these words, pledged the complete protection of the sages in the Daṇḍaka forest, O daughter of Janaka."

sanskrit: saṃśrutya ca na śakṣyāmi jīvamānaḥ pratiśravam munīnām anyathā kartuṃ satyam iṣṭaṃ hi me sadā
english: "Having pledged, I am not able, while living, to act otherwise than my promise to the sages — truth is ever dear to me."

sanskrit: apy ahaṃ jīvitaṃ jahyāṃ tvāṃ vā sīte salakṣmaṇām na tu pratijñāṃ saṃśrutya brāhmaṇebhyo viśeṣataḥ
english: "I would sooner abandon my life, or even you, O Sītā, along with Lakṣmaṇa, than a pledge once given — and especially one given to brāhmaṇas."

sanskrit: tad avaśyaṃ mayā kāryam ṛṣīṇāṃ paripālanam anuktenāpi vaidehi pratijñāya tu kiṃ punaḥ
english: "Therefore the protection of the sages must necessarily be done by me, O Vaidehī — even if I had not spoken, and how much more having made a solemn pledge?"

sanskrit: mama snehāc ca sauhārdād idam uktaṃ tvayā vacaḥ parituṣṭo 'smy ahaṃ sīte na hy aniṣṭo 'nuśiṣyate sadṛśaṃ cānurūpaṃ ca kulasya tava śobhane
english: "These words you have spoken to me out of love and affection; I am pleased, O Sītā — for one dear is not instructed against what is right. It is fitting and befitting your lineage, O beautiful one."

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā vacanaṃ mahātmā sītāṃ priyāṃ maithila rājaputrīm rāmo dhanuṣmān sahalakṣmaṇena jagāma ramyāṇi tapovanāni
english: Having spoken these words, the great-souled Rāma, bearing his bow, together with Lakṣmaṇa, departed with his beloved Sītā, princess of Mithilā, into the beautiful hermitage-forests.
